nodes.statement: The Hard-core model is a probability distribution over the independent sets sigma of an underlying graph G such that each sigma gets probability mass mu(sigma), which is proportional to lambda^abssigma, where abssigma is the cardinality of the independent set sigma.

The Hard-core  model is a probability distribution over  the  {\em independent sets} $\sigma$ of an underlying graph $G$ such that each 
 $\sigma$  gets probability mass $\mu(\sigma)$,  which is proportional to $\lambda^{\abs{\sigma}}$, where $\abs{\sigma}$ 
is the cardinality of the independent  set $\sigma$.

\label{thrm:Ising4SPRadiusAdj}
For $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$, $\lambda>0$, ${\varrho}>1$ and integer ${\Delta} >1$, 
consider graph $G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree ${\Delta}$ such that $\norm{{\UpA}_G}{2}={\varrho}$.

Let $\mu$ be the Ising model on $G$ with external field $\lambda$ and inverse temperature $\beta\in {\mathbb{U}_{\rm Ising}}({\varrho},\varepsilon)$. 

There is a constant $C={C( {\Delta},{\varrho}, \varepsilon)}$ such that the mixing time of Glauber dynamics 
on $\mu$ is at most $C n\log n$.

\label{def:HContraction}
Let $\delta\geq 0$ and the integer ${\Delta}\geq 1$. Also, let $\beta,\gamma, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}$ be
such that $0\leq \beta\leq \gamma$, 
$\gamma >0$ and $\lambda>0$. 

The set of functions $\{ H_d\}_{1\leq d <{\Delta}}$, defined as in \eqref{eq:DefOfH}
with respect to the parameters $\beta,\gamma,\lambda$,
exhibits {\em $\delta$-contraction } if it satisfies the following condition: 

For any $1\leq d < {\Delta}$ and any $({\bf \cadmiumgreen{y}}_1, \ldots, {\bf \cadmiumgreen{y}}_{d})\in [-\infty,+\infty]^{d}$, we have 
$\norm{\nabla H_{d} ({\bf \cadmiumgreen{y}}_1, \ldots, {\bf \cadmiumgreen{y}}_{d})}{\infty} \leq \delta.$

nodes.statement: Let upphi_1 be the principal eigenvector of UpA_G, while let upxi_1 be the corresponding eigenvalue. Since G is assumed to be connected, matrix UpA_G is non-negative and irreducible. The Perron-Frobenius theorem implies varrho &=upxi_1& and && upphi_1(u)>0 forall uin Venspace. Let Upxi be the (Vsetminus Lambda)times (Vsetminus Lambda) diagonal matrix such that for any uin Vsetminus Lambda, we have Upxi(u,u)=upphi_1(u) enspace. Crefeq:PFT4thrm:AdjacencyPotentialSpIn implies that Upxi is non-singular. We prove Crefthrm:AdjacencyPotentialSpIn by applying Crefthrm:InflNormBound4GeneralD, where UpD=Upxi^1/darkmagentas. Specifically, we show that norm Upxi^-1/darkmagentas cdot I^Lambda, tau_G cdot Upxi^1/darkmagentasinfty &leq 1+c cdot Delta^1-(1/darkmagentas)cdot varrho^1/darkmagentas cdot sumnolimits_ ell geq 0 (delta cdot varrho)^ell/darkmagentas enspace. Then, Crefthrm:AdjacencyPotentialSpIn follows by substituting c=fraczetavarrho and delta=frac1-varepsilonvarrho and noting that the norm on the l.h.s. is an upper bound for rho( I^Lambda,tau_G). It remains to show that is true. For win Vsetminus Lambda, we let mathboldq(w) be equal to the absolute row sum for the row of matrix Upxi^-1/darkmagentas cdot I^Lambda, tau_G cdot Upxi^1/darkmagentas that corresponds to vertex w. Crefthrm:InflNormBound4GeneralD and imply mathboldq(w) & leq 1+ fraccleft(upphi_1(w)right)^1/darkmagentas cdot left( sumnolimits_z in N(w)left(upphi_1(z)right)^1/darkmagentas+ sumnolimits_ell geq 2 left( delta^ell-1 cdot left(UpCcdotUpA^ell-1_Gcdot upphi_1right) (wz) right)^1/darkmagentas right) enspace. Recalling that upphi_1 is the principal eigenvector of UpA_G, implies UpCcdotUpA^ell-1_Gcdot upphi_1 &= varrho^ell-1 cdot UpCcdot upphi_1enspace. Plugging the above into and rearranging, we get mathboldq(w) & =1+ c cdot sumnolimits_ellgeq 1 left(delta cdot varrho right)^(ell-1)/darkmagentas cdot sumnolimits_zin N_G(w)left( textstyle fracupphi_1(z)upphi_1(w) right)^1/darkmagentas enspace. We need to bound the rightmost sum in the equation above. Letting d=absN_G(w) and applying H\"older's inequality, we get sumnolimits_zin N_G(w)left( textstylefracupphi_1(z) upphi_1(w) right)^1/darkmagentas & leq left( sumnolimits _zin N_G(w) textstyle fracupphi_1(z) upphi_1(w) right)^1/darkmagentas d^1-(1/darkmagentas)\ = \ Delta^1-(1/darkmagentas) cdot varrho^1/darkmagentasenspace, where the last equality follows from the observations that sum_zin N_G(w)upphi_1(z)=varrhocdot upphi_1(w) and d^1-(1/darkmagentas)leq Delta^1-(1/darkmagentas). Plugging into we get mathboldq(w) &leq 1+ c cdot Delta^1-(1/darkmagentas) cdot varrho^1/darkmagentas cdot sumnolimits_ell geq 0 left(delta cdot varrho right)^ell/darkmagentas enspace . nonumber The above holds for any win Vsetminus Lambda, implying that is true. Crefthrm:AdjacencyPotentialSpIn follows.

Our assumptions for the potential function ${\Psi}$ imply that, for every $e_{i}\in P$, we have $\uppsi(e_{i})\neq 0$. 

Using a simple telescopic trick, we get 
\begin{align}
\abs{{\tt weight}(P)}&= \prod^{\ell}_{i=1}\frac{\uppsi(e_{i})}{\uppsi(e_{i})} \cdot \abs{\upalpha(e_{i})} \ 
 = \ \uppsi(e_{\ell})\cdot \frac{\abs{\upalpha(e_1)}}{\uppsi(e_1)}\cdot \prod^{\ell}_{i=2}\frac{\uppsi(e_{i-1})}{\uppsi(e_{i})}\cdot \abs{\upalpha(e_{i})} \enspace. \nonumber
\end{align}
The claim follows.

nodes.statement: For brevity, we let nonumber tt Max& =max_bare, hate in T left\ textstyle uppsi(bare) cdot fracabsupalpha(hate) uppsi(hate) right\ enspace. Recall that ell>1. From the definition of H_ell in and Crefclaim:AddPotentialA we have H_ell &= sumnolimits_uin Vsetminus Lambda sumnolimits_P=(e_1,ldots, e_ell) in P(u, ell) left( uppsi(e_ell)cdot fracabsupalpha(e_1) uppsi(e_1) right)cdot prodnolimits_2leq ileq ellfracuppsi(e_i-1)uppsi(e_i)cdot absupalpha(e_i) cdot UpD(u) enspace. nonumber For uin Vsetminus Lambda and ellgeq 0, recall that P(u,ell) is the set of paths P from the root of T to the set of copies of vertex u which are at level ell of the tree such that tt weight(P)neq 0. Also, recall that tt A(u,ell) is the set of copies of u at level ell in T that are connected to the root with a path Pin P(u,ell). Noting that left( uppsi(e_ell)cdot fracabsupalpha(e_1)uppsi(e_1) right)leq tt Max, we get H_ell &leq tt Maxcdot sumnolimits_uin Vsetminus Lambda sumnolimits_P=(e_1,ldots, e_ell) in P(u, ell) prodnolimits_2leq ileq ellfracuppsi(e_i-1)uppsi(e_i)cdot absupalpha(e_i)cdot UpD(u) enspace. As far as R^(ell)_root is concerned, recalling , we have R^(ell)_root &= tt Maxcdot sumnolimits_1leq jleq r R^(ell)_z_j enspace, where z_1, ldots, z_r are the children of the root, for some integer r>0. We show that for any vertex v at level h=1,ldots, ell-1 of the tree T, we have R^(ell)_v &=sumnolimits_uin Vsetminus Lambda sumnolimits_P=(e_1,ldots, e_ell-h+1)in P(v,u, ell) prodnolimits_2leq ileq ell-h+1 fracuppsi(e_i-1) uppsi(e_i) cdot absupalpha(e_i) cdot UpD(u) enspace, where P(v,u, ell) is the set of paths of length ell-h+1 from the parent of vertex v to tt A(u,ell)cap T_v. Before proving that is true, let us show how it implies Crefclaim:CEllVsCalD. For every child z_j of the root, implies R^(ell)_z_j & = sumnolimits_uin Vsetminus Lambda sumnolimits_P=(e_1,ldots, e_ell) in P(z_j, u, ell) prodnolimits_2leq ileq ell fracuppsi(e_i-1)uppsi(e_i)cdot absupalpha(e_i) cdot UpD(u) enspace. Summing the above over all the children of the root, we get sumnolimits_z_j R^(ell)_z_j & = sumnolimits_uin Vsetminus Lambda sumnolimits_P=(e_1,ldots e_ell) in P(u, ell) prodnolimits_2leq ileq ell fracuppsi(e_i-1)uppsi(e_i)cdot absupalpha(e_i) cdot UpD(u) enspace. For the above, we use the observation that the sets P(z_j,u,ell)'s partition P(u,ell), i.e., we have cup_z_jP(z_j,u,ell)=P(u,ell), while for distinct j, i the sets P(z_j,u,ell) and P(z_i,u,ell) do not intersect. Plugging into , we see that R^(ell)_root is equal to the r.h.s. of the inequality in . This implies that H_ell leq R^(ell)_root, which also proves the claim. We conclude the proof of Crefclaim:CEllVsCalD by showing that is true. To this end, we use induction on the level h of vertex v in . The basis of the induction corresponds to taking h=ell-1. For the inductive step, we assume that there is hleq ell-1 such that that is true. We then prove that is also true for any vertex v at level h-1 of tree T. We start with the basis and show for a vertex v at level ell-1. As per standard notation, let v_1, ldots, v_d be the children of v. These children are vertices at level ell. From and , we have R^(ell)_v &= sumnolimits_jfracuppsi(b_v )uppsi(b_j)cdot abs upalpha(b_j) cdot R^(ell)_v_j nonumber\\ &=sumnolimits_u in Vsetminus Lambda sumnolimits_jfracuppsi(b_v )uppsi(b_j)cdot abs upalpha(b_j) cdot mathds1\v_j in tt A (u,ell )\cdot UpD(u) enspace, where we let b_v be the edge that connects v to its parent at T, while edge b_j connects v to its child v_j. For the second equality, we substitute R^(ell)_v_j by using . For each u in Vsetminus Lambda in , the summand fracuppsi(b_v )uppsi(b_j)cdot absupalpha(b_j) cdot mathds1\v_j in tt A (u,ell )\ is non-zero only if the edges b_v and b_j form a path which belongs to set P(v,u,ell), i.e., we have (b_v,b_j)in P(v,u,ell). We use this observation and write as follows: R^(ell)_v&=sumnolimits_u in Vsetminus Lambda sumnolimits_P=(e_1,e_2) in P(v, u, ell) fracuppsi(e_1) uppsi(e_2) cdot absupalpha(e_2) cdot UpD(u) enspace. It is not hard to see that corresponds to for h=ell-1. This concludes the proof of the base of the induction. The induction hypothesis is that there exists 1<hleq ell-1, such that is true for any vertex at level h of tree T. We show that the hypothesis implies that is true for any vertex v at level h-1. As per standard notation, we let v_1, ldots, v_d be the children of v, while edge b_v connects v to its parent and edge b_j connects v to its child v_j. From we have R^(ell)_v &= sumnolimits_j fracuppsi(b_v )uppsi(b_j)cdot absupalpha(b_j) cdot R^(ell)_v_j enspace. nonumber The children of v are at level h. Using the hypothesis, we substitute each R^(ell)_v_j using and get nonumber R^(ell)_v&= sumnolimits_uin Vsetminus Lambda sumnolimits_j fracuppsi(b_v )uppsi(b_j)cdot absupalpha(b_j)cdot sumnolimits_P=(e_1,ldots, e_ell-h+1)in P(v_j, u, ell) prodnolimits_2leq ileq ell-h+1 fracuppsi(e_i-1) uppsi(e_i) cdot absupalpha(e_i) cdot UpD(u) enspace. It is elementary that for any 1leq jleq d and for every path P=(e_1,ldots, e_ell-h+1)in P(v_j, u, ell), there is exactly one path Q=(overlinee_1, ldots, overlinee_ell-h+2)in P(v,u,ell), with overlinee_2=\v,v_j \, such that nonumber prodnolimits_2leq ileq ell-h+2 fracuppsi(overlinee_i-1) uppsi(overlinee_i) cdot absupalpha(overlinee_i) &= fracuppsi(b_v )uppsi(b_j)cdot absupalpha(b_j) cdot prodnolimits_2leq ileq ell-h+1 fracuppsi(e_i-1) uppsi(e_i) cdot absupalpha(e_i) enspace and vice versa. Combining the two relations above, we get R^(ell)_v&= sumnolimits_uin Vsetminus Lambda sumnolimits_Q=(overlinee_1,ldots, overlinee_ell-h+2)in P(v, u, ell) prodnolimits_2leq ileq ell-h+2 fracuppsi(overlinee_i-1) uppsi(overlinee_i) cdot absupalpha(overlinee_i) cdot UpD(u) enspace, nonumber which proves the inductive steps and concludes the inductive proof. Crefclaim:CEllVsCalD follows.

\label{thrm:InflVsExtInfl}
Let ${\Delta}> 1$ and $k> 0$, let $\beta,\gamma, \lambda, b \in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $\gamma >0$,
$0\leq \beta\leq \gamma, \lambda>0$ and $b>0$. 

Let $G=(V,E)$ be of maximum degree ${\Delta}$. Consider $\mu_G$ the Gibbs distribution on $G$ 
specified by the parameters $(\beta, \gamma, \lambda)$, 
while assume that $\mu_G$ is $b$-marginally
bounded.

There is a constant $\widehat{C}>0$ such that, for any $\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$, 
there is an $\iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}\times \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda, k }$ matrix ${\mathcal{N}}$ over $\mathbb{R}$, 
for which we have

\begin{align}\label{eq:thrm:InflVsExtInfl}
 {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_G& =\UpD_{k} \cdot \left( \applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}\circ {\mathcal{N}} \right )\cdot \UpC_{k}
+ {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G, <2k} \enspace, 
\end{align}
while for any $P,Q\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ we also have $\abs{{\mathcal{N}}(P,Q)}  \leq \widehat{C}$.


Recall that $\applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}\circ {\mathcal{N}}$ is the Hadamard product of the two matrices. 
Matrix ${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G, <2k}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:DefOfCISmallerK}.

\label{thrm:InfNormBoundHConj}
Let ${\Delta} > 1$ and $k,N\geq 1$ be integers, $c>0$, $\uprho> 1$, $\darkmagenta{s}\geq 1$ while 
let $b,\varepsilon\in (0,1)$. Also, let $\beta,\gamma, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $\gamma >0$,
$0\leq \beta\leq \gamma$ and $\lambda>0$. 


Consider graph $G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree ${\Delta}$ such that 

$\nnorm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^N}{1/N}{2}= \uprho$.

Assume that $\mu_G$, the Gibbs distribution on $G$ specified by the parameters $(\beta, \gamma, \lambda)$,
is $b$-marginally bounded.

For $\delta= \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho}$, suppose that there
is a $(\darkmagenta{s},\delta,c)$-potential function ${\Psi}$ with respect to $(\beta,\gamma,\lambda)$. 


There exists a fixed constant $\widehat{c} \geq 1$ such that 
for any $\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$, the extended influence matrix 
$\applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}$, that is induced by $\mu^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$, satisfies that
\begin{align}\nonumber
\norm{  \abs{ \applegreen{{\mathcal{L}}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_{G,k}}}{2\darkmagenta{s}} &\leq \widehat{c}\cdot \sum\nolimits_{\ell\geq k} 
\left(
 {\textstyle \left(\frac{1-\varepsilon/2}{\uprho}\right)^{\ell} } \cdot 

\norm{ ( \cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^{\ell}}{2} 
 \right)^{1/\darkmagenta{s}}
\enspace.
\end{align}

nodes.statement: For what follows, we abbreviate applegreenL^Lambda,tau_G,k to rosegoldL. Consider P, Qin irisE_Lambda,k which are compatible. Let w and u be the starting vertices of P and Q, respectively. Then, as already noticed in , we have rosegoldL(P,Q)&=I^P,Q(w,u), & and && rosegoldL(Q,P)&=I^P,Q(u, w)enspace, where the influence matrix I^P,Q is with respect to upzeta^P,Q, the \P, Q\-extension of mu^Lambda,tau_G. Note that I^P,Q and I^Q,P correspond to the same influence matrix. A useful observation is that Crefclaim:InfSymmetrisation and imply that if upzeta^P,Q_w(+1), upzeta^P,Q_u(+1)notin \0,1\, then we have sqrt fracupzeta^P,Q_w(+1) cdot upzeta^P,Q_w(-1) upzeta^P,Q_u(+1) cdot upzeta^P,Q_u(-1) cdot rosegoldL(P,Q)&= sqrtfracupzeta^P,Q_u(+1) cdot upzeta^P,Q_u(-1) upzeta^P,Q_w(+1) cdot upzeta^P,Q_w(-1) cdot rosegoldL(Q,P)enspace. If at least one of upzeta^P,Q_w(+1), upzeta^P,Q_u(+1) is in \0,1\, then we have rosegoldL(P,Q)=rosegoldL(Q,P)=0. Let the irisE_Lambda,ktimes irisE_Lambda,k matrix M be defined as follows: For P in irisE_Lambda,k with starting vertex w and Q in irisE_Lambda,k with starting vertex u, such that P and Q are compatible while upzeta^P,Q_w(+1), upzeta^P,Q_u(+1)notin \0,1\, we let M(P,Q)&= sqrt fracupzeta^P,Q_w(+1) cdot upzeta^P,Q_w(-1) upzeta^P,Q_u(+1) cdot upzeta^P,Q_u(-1) cdot absrosegoldL(P, Q) enspace. On the other hand, if at least one of upzeta^P,Q_w(+1), upzeta^P,Q_u(+1) is in \0,1\, then we let M(P,Q)=0. Also, we let M(P,Q)=0 when P and Q are not compatible. M has non-negative entries, while implies that it is symmetric. Furthermore, we have norm absrosegoldL2 &leq b^-2 cdot norm M 2 leq b^-2 cdot norm M2darkmagentas leq b^-4 cdot norm absrosegoldL2darkmagentas enspace. The first inequality follows by noting that and the b-marginal boundedness assumption imply that absrosegoldL leq b^-2 cdot M, where the comparison is entry-wise. The second inequality follows since M is symmetric. Similarly to the first inequality, the third inequality follows by noting that and the b-marginal boundedness assumption imply that M has non-negative entries, while M leq b^-2cdot absrosegoldL, where the comparison is entry-wise. Crefclaim:Ll2VsLl2s follows for c_3=b^-4.

\label{prop:StableSSM}
Let ${\Delta} > 1$, $k\geq 1$ and $N>1$ be integers, $c>0$, $\uprho> 1$, $\darkmagenta{s} \geq 1$, while 
let $b,\varepsilon\in (0,1)$. Also, let $\beta,\gamma, \lambda\in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $\gamma >0$,
$0\leq \beta\leq \gamma$ and $\lambda>0$. 


Consider graph $G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree ${\Delta}$ such that 
$\nnorm{ (\cadmiumgreen{\UpH}_{G,k})^N}{1/N}{2}= \uprho$.

Assume that $\mu$, the Gibbs distribution on $G$ specified by the parameters $(\beta, \gamma, \lambda)$,
is $b$-marginally bounded.

For $\delta= \frac{1-\varepsilon}{\uprho}$, suppose that there
is a $(\darkmagenta{s},\delta,c)$-potential function ${\Psi}$ with respect to $(\beta,\gamma,\lambda)$. 

There exists a bounded number $\ell_0>2k$ such that, 
for any $\Lambda\subset V$ and $\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda}$,
for any $u,w\in V\setminus \Lambda$ with ${\rm dist}(u,w)\geq 2k$ and for $P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}$ 
that emanates from  $w$  the following is true:


For any edge $f$ in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P}, u)$ which is at distance $\ell\geq \ell_0$ from $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, we have 
\begin{align}\label{eq:prop:StableSSM}
\upalpha_{P}(f)&\leq (1+\varepsilon/3)^{1/\darkmagenta{s}} \cdot \upalpha(f) \enspace, 
\end{align}
where the set $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$ and the weights $\{ \upalpha_{P}(e)\}$, $\{\upalpha(e)\}$ are specified above.

nodes.statement: We consider path W=e_1,ldots, e_ell from the root of overlinecadmiumgreenT=T_SAW(gextGP, u) to a copy of vertex w. Note that we specify W it terms of its edges. Recall the two sets of edge-weights for overlinecadmiumgreenT, i.e., set \upalpha(e)\ is induced by the Gibbs distribution mu^M,sigma_applegreenT, and set \ upalpha_P(e)\ is induced by the Gibbs distribution mu^L,eta_overlinecadmiumgreenT. Also, recall that set magentaoverlinett A_P consists of each vertex in overlinecadmiumgreenT which is either a copy of a vertex vin P, or a copy of a split-vertex of vin P. Let upalpha_min=min_e\ absupalpha_P (e), absupalpha(e) \, where e varies over the set of edges in overlinecadmiumgreenT such that upalpha_P (e), upalpha(e)neq 0. Similarly, we define upalpha_max=max_e\absupalpha_P(e), absupalpha(e)\ where e varies over the same set of edges. It is an easy exercise to show that our assumption about b-marginal boundedness, for fixed b>0, implies that upalpha_min and upalpha_max are constants bounded away from zero. Consider ell_0 as specified in Crefprop:StableSSM. Let set H consist of the edges e_i in W such that i>ell-k. Also, let set K consist of the edges e_iin W such that 1leq i leq ell-k and dist(e_i, magentaoverlinett A_P )<ell_0. Similarly, let set R consist of the edges e_iin W such that 1leq i leq ell-k and dist(e_i, magentaoverlinett A_P )geq ell_0. We have prodnolimits_1leq ileq ellabsupalpha_P(e_i) &= prodnolimits_e_iin Habsupalpha_P(e_i) cdot prodnolimits_e_i in Kabsupalpha_P(e_i) cdot prodnolimits_e_i in Rabsupalpha_P(e_i) enspace. For our subsequent arguments, we use the following result. For W=e_1,ldots, e_ell and \upalpha_P(e_i)\, \upalpha(e_i)\, the following is true: if upalpha_P(e_i)neq 0, then we have upalpha(e_i)neq 0, for each e_iin Kcup R. For upalpha_P(e_i) such that e_iin H, we use the standard bound absupalpha_P(e_i) &leq 1enspace. For each edge e_iin K, we have abs upalpha_P(e_i) leq fracupalpha_maxupalpha_min cdot absupalpha(e_i) \ leq \ (1+varepsilon/3)^1/darkmagentas cdot fracupalpha_maxupalpha_min cdot absupalpha(e_i) enspace. We use Crefclaim:SupportOfWeiS for the first inequality. The second inequality uses that 1<(1+varepsilon/2)^1/darkmagentas for varepsilon, darkmagentas>0. Crefprop:StableSSM implies that, for every e_i in R, we have abs upalpha_P(e_i) leq (1+varepsilon/3)^1/darkmagentascdot abs upalpha(e_i) enspace. Plugging , and into , we get prod^ell_i=1 absupalpha_P(e_i) &leq left( fracupalpha_maxupalpha_min right)^absK cdot prod^ell-k_i=1 (1+varepsilon/3)^1/s cdot absupalpha(e_i)enspace. For the cardinality of set K, we use the following claim. There are at most (k+1)cdot Delta^ell_0+1 edges in path W that are at distance <ell_0 from set magentaoverlinett A_P. The above implies that absKleq (k+1) cdot Delta^ell_0+1. Hence, Crefthrm:ProdWideHatBetaVsBeta follows from by setting widehatc_1=left( fracupalpha_maxupalpha_min right)^(k+1)cdot Delta^ell_0+1.

We use \Cref{lemma:Subtree4TSawU} and identify $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=T_{\rm SAW}(\gext{G}{P},u)$ as a subtree of $\applegreen{T}=T_{\rm SAW}(G,u)$
such that both trees have  the same root. Then, $W$ is also a path in $\applegreen{T}$ starting from the root. 


Having $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ as a subtree of $\applegreen{T}$, we endow the subset of edges of  $\applegreen{T}$ that correspond to those of $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$
with the edge weights $\{\upalpha_{P}(e)\}$. Note that  we do not necessarily  have $\upalpha_{P}(e)$ for all edges $e\in \applegreen{T}$.

Also,  recall that the set of weights $\{\upalpha(e)\}$  and $\{\upalpha_{P}(e)\}$ are induced by 
$\mu^{M,\sigma}_{\applegreen{T}}$ and  $\mu^{L,\eta}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$, respectively. 

For $e_{i}\in W$, let  $e_{i}=\{x_{i},z_{i}\}$ 
while let $\uppi_{i}$ be the set  that consists of $x_{i}, z_{i}$ and their 
children in $\applegreen{T}$.

Furthermore, we have the following observations:
 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item \Cref{lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU} implies that $\byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}\cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, \label{obs:APBarTVsBarAp}
\item \Cref{lemma:Subtree4TSawU} implies that each vertex in $\applegreen{T} \setminus \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ corresponds to a descendant of a vertex in $\byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}$, \label{obs:TminusBarTVsAp}
\item \Cref{lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU} implies that $M \cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}} \subseteq L$, \label{obs:PinMVsBarTVsPinL}
\item \Cref{lemma:BoundaryTVsBoundaryTPFromU} implies that the pinnings $\sigma$ and $\eta$ agree on the assignment  in $L\cap M$. \label{obs:PinMVsPinLIntesection}
\end{enumerate}
Since we assume that our Gibbs distributions are $b$-marginally bounded,  we can have $\upalpha(e_{i})=0$ (resp. $\upalpha_{P}(e_{i})=0$) only if at least one vertex in
$\uppi_{i}$ has a fixed configuration under $\mu^{M,\sigma}_{\applegreen{T}}$ (resp. $\mu^{L,\eta}_{\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}}$).
Note that for Gibbs  distributions with parameter $\beta=0$, it is possible that  a pinning on a child of $x_{i}$ or   $z_{i}$ 
determines  the configuration of its parent with probability 1, implying that  $\upalpha(e_{i})=0$ (resp. $\upalpha_{P}(e_{i})=0$). 



Consider $1\leq i \leq \ell-k$. If there is $v\in \uppi_{i}$ which  is not in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$, this means that at least one of 
$x_{i}$ and $z_{i}$ is  in $\byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}$, i.e., due to observation \ref{obs:TminusBarTVsAp}. 
But then, since $x_{i},z_{i}\in \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$,  observation \ref{obs:APBarTVsBarAp} implies  that the parent of $v$, i.e., one of  $x_{i}, z_{i}$, 
is in $\byzantine{{\tt A}}_{P}\cap \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}=\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$. 
Since $i\leq \ell-k$,  if any of $x_{i},z_{i}$  is in  $\magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$, then it should be  a split-vertex in $\cadmiumgreen{\UpS}_{P}$, which means that is of degree $1$. 
This can only happen if $i=1$, however in this case we  have  $x_{i},z_{i}\notin \magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$ because the root is a copy of vertex $u$ which is
at distance at least $k$ from any copy of a vertex $v\in \magenta{\overline{{\tt A}}}_{P}$. We then conclude that this event cannot happen. 

Hence,  all elements in $\uppi_{i}$ are vertices in $\overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$. The fact that $e_{i}\in \overline{\cadmiumgreen{T}}$ and 
observations \ref{obs:PinMVsBarTVsPinL} and \ref{obs:PinMVsPinLIntesection} imply that  if any vertex in $\uppi_{i}$ is pinned, then the
pinning is the same under both $\sigma,\eta$. Hence,  if  $\upalpha_{P}(e_{i})\neq 0$, then we also have that $\upalpha(e_{i})\neq 0$. 

\Cref{claim:SupportOfWeiS} follows.

Applying the same arguments as in the proof of Creflemma:FromCalI2CalF, we obtain max_Q,z\ |widehatN_A(Q,z)\| leq C_A, where C_A is specified in the statement of Creflemma:FromCalI2CalF. Note that the bound C_A depends only on the parameters k and b for the marginal boundedness. Crefclaim:CFReverseSplit follows.

nodes.name: Proof of \Cref{lemma:TsawPVsTsaw}
nodes.statement: Our result follows by showing that there is an appropriate bijection cadmiumorangeuph from the vertex set of caprit_P to that of blueT_P that allows us to identify caprit_P with blueT_P. Since the vertices in caprit_P correspond to the walks in magentaOmega and the vertices in blueT_P correspond to the walks in magentaOmega_P, we equivalently establish the bijection cadmiumorangeuph from set magentaOmega to magentaOmega_P. For concreteness, let P=x_0, ldots, x_k, while x_0=w. Let set O consist of each edge e in G, which does not connect two consecutive vertices in P but has at least one end in the set \x_0, ldots, x_k-1\. Similarly, let set O_P consist of each edge in gextGP which is between a split-vertex in set cadmiumgreenUpS_P and another vertex of gextGP. The only edges in G that do not appear in gextGP are exactly those in set O. Similarly, the only edges in gextGP that do not appear in G are exactly those in set O_P. This implies that the elements in magentaOmega cap magentaOmega_P correspond to the walks that do not use edges from sets O and O_P. The definitions of the two trees caprit_P and blueT_P imply that nonumber magentaOmega^(a)&=magentaOmega^(a)_P & and &&magentaOmega^(c)&=magentaOmega^(c)_P enspace. To see this, recall that we have P=x_0, ldots, x_k. Then each W=v_0, ldots, v_r in magentaOmega^(a) corresponds to a self-avoiding walk that emanates from vertex w, while v_i=x_i, for i=0,ldots, min\k,r \. It is immediate to check that each such walk W also belongs to magentaOmega^(a)_P and vice versa. This implies that magentaOmega^(a)=magentaOmega^(a)_P. With a very similar argument, we also get magentaOmega^(c)=magentaOmega^(c)_P. It is only the walks in magentaOmega^(b) and magentaOmega^(b)_P that use edges from O and O_P, respectively. We start with $\norm{ \UpD_{k}}{2}$. 

Consider the product $\UpD_{k} \cdot \MTR{\UpD}_{k}$, where $\MTR{\UpD}_{k}$ is the matrix transpose of $\UpD_{k}$. 

Matrix $\UpD_{k} \cdot \MTR{\UpD}_{k}$ is $(V\setminus \Lambda)\times (V\setminus \Lambda)$, while for  any $u,w\in V\setminus \Lambda$, we have 
\begin{align}
\left (\UpD_{k} \cdot \MTR{\UpD}_{k} \right)(u,w) 
& = \sum\nolimits_{P \in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}} \UpD_{k}(u, P)\times \MTR{\UpD}_{k}(P, w) \nonumber\\
& = \sum\nolimits_{P \in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}} \mathds{1}\{\textrm{$u$ is the starting vertex in $P$} \} \times \mathds{1}\{\textrm{$w$ is the starting vertex in $P$} \} \nonumber\\
& = \mathds{1}\{ w=u\} \times \sum\nolimits_{P\in \iris{{\mathcal{E}}}_{\Lambda,k}} \mathds{1}\{\textrm{$u$ is the starting vertex in $P$} \} \nonumber\\
&\leq \mathds{1}\{ w=u\} \times {\Delta}^{k} \enspace. \nonumber
\end{align}

We conclude that $\UpD_{k} \cdot \MTR{\UpD}_{k}$ is a non-negative and diagonal matrix. For $w\in V\setminus \Lambda$, we have 
$(\UpD_{k} \cdot \MTR{\UpD}_{k} )(w,w) \leq {\Delta}^{k}$. 

Hence, we have $ \norm{ \UpD_{k} \cdot \MTR{\UpD}_{k}}{2} \leq {\Delta}^{k}$, which implies that  $\norm{ \UpD_{k}}{2} \leq {\Delta}^{k/2}$.

Working similarly, we get $ \norm{ \UpC_{k}}{2}\leq {\Delta}^{k/2}$.
 \Cref{claim:2NormBoundforVVsEdge-AAA} follows.

Let $\Upsigma^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ be the $(V\times \Lambda)\times (V\times \Lambda)$ covariance matrix defined with respect to $\mu^{\Lambda, \tau}$. That is, for any $u,v\in V\setminus \Lambda$ we have 
\begin{align}\nonumber
\Upsigma^{\Lambda,\tau}_G(v,u) &=\mu^{\Lambda, \tau}_{(v,u)}((+1,+1))-\mu^{\Lambda, \tau}_{v}(+1)\cdot \mu^{\Lambda, \tau}_{u}(+1)\enspace. 
\end{align}
A straightforward observation is that $\Upsigma^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ is symmetric. W.l.o.g. in this proof, assume that 
the diagonal entries of $\Upsigma^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ are non-zero. 

Note that for any $v\in V\setminus \Lambda$ we have that
\begin{align}\label{eq:UpMVsCovMat}
\UpM(v,v)= \sqrt{\Upsigma^{\Lambda,\tau}_G(v,v)}\enspace. 
\end{align}
Furthermore, it is standard to show, e.g. see \cite{VigodaSpectralInd}, that $\Upsigma^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ and 
${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ satisfy that 

${\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_G(u,v)= \frac{\Upsigma^{\Lambda,\tau}_G(u,v)}{\Upsigma^{\Lambda,\tau}_G(u,u)}.$ 

Since $\Upsigma^{\Lambda,\tau}_G$ is symmetric, this relation implies that
\begin{align}\nonumber
\Upsigma^{\Lambda,\tau}_G(u,u) \cdot {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_G(u,v) &
=\Upsigma^{\Lambda,\tau}_G(v,v) \cdot {\mathcal{I}}^{\Lambda,\tau}_G(v,u) \enspace.

We have that 
\begin{align} \nonumber
{\bf x}^T (\byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell} \cdot \UpR){\bf x}&=\frac{1}{2}\left((\byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell} \cdot \UpR)(P,Q^{-1}) 
+(\byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell} \cdot \UpR)(Q^{-1}, Q^{-1})+(\byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell} \cdot \UpR)(P,P)+

\end{align}
Recalling the definition of matrix $\byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell}\cdot \UpR$, we have 
\begin{align} \nonumber
\byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell}(P,Q) =(\byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell}\cdot \UpR)(P,Q^{-1})=(\byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell} \cdot \UpR)(Q^{-1},P) \enspace,

\end{align}
The last inequality above follows from the fact that $\byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell}\cdot \UpR$ is symmetric, with maximum
eigenvalue $\sigma_{k,\ell}$.

Let the integers $t=\lfloor \frac{\ell}{N} \rfloor$ and $r\geq 0$ be such that $\ell= N\cdot t+r$.
We have 
\begin{align}\label{eq:Base4lemma:SingSequenConv}
\left( \upsigma_{k,\ell} \right)^{1/\ell}& = \nnorm{  \byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell}}{\frac{1}{\ell}}{2} \leq 
\nnorm{  \byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell-r}}{\frac{1}{\ell}}{2} \cdot \nnorm{  \byzantine{\UpH}^{r}}{\frac{1}{\ell}}{2} \leq 
\nnorm{  \byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell-r}}{\frac{1}{\ell-r}}{2} \cdot \nnorm{ \byzantine{\UpH}^{r}}{\frac{1}{\ell}}{2} \enspace. 
\end{align}
Furthermore, noting that $\ell-r=N\cdot t$, we get 
\begin{align}
\nnorm{  \byzantine{\UpH}^{\ell-r}}{\frac{1}{\ell-r}}{2} &= \nnorm{ \byzantine{\UpH}^{N\cdot t}}{\frac{1}{N\cdot t}}{2} \leq 
\nnorm{ \byzantine{\UpH}^N}{\frac{1}{N}}{2} = (\upsigma_{k,N})^{\frac{1}{N}}\enspace. 
\end{align}
Plugging the above into \eqref{eq:Base4lemma:SingSequenConv} we have
\begin{align}\nonumber
\left( \upsigma_{k,\ell} \right)^{1/\ell}& \leq (\upsigma_{k,N})^{\frac{1}{N}} 
\cdot \nnorm{  \byzantine{\UpH}^{r}}{\frac{1}{\ell}}{2} \enspace.
\end{align}
Noting that $\nnorm{ \byzantine{\UpH}^{r}}{\frac{1}{\ell}}{2}\leq ({\Delta}-1)^{\frac{r}{\ell}}$
and recalling that ${\Delta}$ is bounded, there is fixed $\ell_0$ such that 
for $\ell>\ell_0$ we have $\nnorm{ \byzantine{\UpH}^r}{\frac{1}{\ell}}{2}\leq (1+z)$.

\Cref{lemma:SingSequenConv} follows.
